title: That Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm I Tried: My Skin Hates Spring
body:
Okay so it’s spring. The air is doing that thing. You know the thing. It’s not cold but it’s not warm, it’s just… dry and weird. Like the inside of an old office building. My face knows it first. Always does. It gets this tight feeling, like I smiled too hard yesterday and my skin forgot how to relax. And then the flaking starts. Not cute snowflake flaking. More like a sad, dusty reptile. Right between my eyebrows. It’s embarrassing. I’d scratch my head and get a little snowstorm. Charming.

So I was sitting there, feeling my forehead, listening to my neighbor’s TV through the wall. Some game show. And I was just done. Done with the lotion that sat on top of my skin like plastic wrap. Done with the expensive serum that did nothing but make my bank account sad. I was scrolling, probably looking at memes, and this thing popped up. A tallow balm. Beef fat. For your face. I laughed. Out loud. My cat looked at me. It sounded insane. But the description said “Bourbon Vanilla” and I don’t know, I was curious. And desperate. My skin was basically yelling at me. So I clicked. It was from some small shop on Etsy. The pictures looked nice. Simple. I figured, what’s the worst that could happen? I already looked like a shedding snake.

**How Beef Tallow Ended Up on My Nightstand**

Look. I need to be clear. I was skeptical. Putting rendered cow fat on my face felt like a step backwards, like something my great-great-grandmother might have done before they invented… everything. I’ve tried it all. The glass bottles with droppers. The creams in fancy jars that cost more than my electric bill. They’d work for a day. Maybe two. Then my skin would go back to being its difficult, parched self. This whole spring skincare search was getting old.

But I kept reading about this tallow stuff. The balm is made from grass-fed beef suet, whipped up. They make it in France. The big thing people say is that it’s similar to the oils our own skin makes. So it doesn’t just sit there—it actually gets in there. My brain went, “Okay, that sort of makes sense.” My nose was still skeptical. Beef-scented face cream? No thanks. But this one was bourbon vanilla. That sounded… less barnyard. I was at the point where I’d try anything. I ordered it on a Tuesday night. I think it was Tuesday. No, wait, it was Thursday. Because the package came on a Monday. Anyway.

**What This Stuff Is Actually Like**

The jar showed up. It’s small. Cute. I opened it and just stared. The texture is weird. In a good way. It’s not a cream. It’s not an oil. It’s this dense, kind of fluffy paste. Like if butter and whipped frosting had a baby. You scoop a tiny bit—and I mean tiny, a little goes so far—and it melts the second it touches your skin. It doesn’t feel greasy. It just… disappears. But your skin feels different. Not shiny. Not sticky. Just sort of quiet. And the smell? It’s not “faintly of” anything. It’s just vanilla. But not cake vanilla. Not candle vanilla. It’s warmer. Deeper. Like vanilla extract you’d cook with, but smoother. It’s cozy. I put it on before bed and it just smells like… comfort. It’s the opposite of stressful. My bathroom smelled nice for hours.

I started using it at night. After I wash my face. Just that. No ten-step routine. Just this balm. I’d put it on the dry spots first—the reptile forehead, the patches by my nose. Then just a little all over. The first morning I woke up and my skin didn’t feel tight. That hadn’t happened in months. Maybe years. I told my sister about it on the phone and she was like, “You’re putting WHAT on your face?” I had to explain. Again.

**Dealing With My Spring Skin Now**

So it’s been a few weeks. The weather is still doing its weird spring thing. Some days are warm, some are windy, the pollen is everywhere. My skin usually freaks out. Total chaos. But right now? It’s just… calm. The flaking is gone. Completely. My face doesn’t have that stretched-canvas feeling anymore. It just feels like skin. Normal, hydrated, not-freaking-out skin. I even started putting a dab on my elbows and knuckles because why not. They’re weirdly soft now. I was doing the dishes yesterday and just noticed my hands looked okay. Not cracked. That’s a win.

This is the part where I’d usually say a product is “good for fine lines” or whatever. I don’t know about that. I’m not looking in the mirror that hard. But my face looks less tired. The dry little lines I’d get from squinting? They’re less… obvious. I guess because the skin is actually hydrated from the inside out, not just coated on top. The tallow balm for spring has been a game-changer. I said it. It sounds dramatic but it’s true. I’m not battling my face every morning. I just get up. It’s wild.

I got the jar from this little Etsy shop. I’m not gonna link it because this isn’t an ad. I just like it. The whole thing feels honest. No crazy promises. Just a simple balm that works. For my dry spring skin, it’s been the only thing that actually helped. I’m probably gonna order another one soon so I don’t run out. The thought of going back to my sad, flaky face is… no. Just no.

**Quick Questions I Get Asked**

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. From what I get, it’s close to what our skin already makes. So it sinks in deep instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin something it actually recognizes. My face seems to think so, anyway.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about that. My skin can get weird. But this hasn’t caused any issues for me. It absorbs so fast it doesn’t really have time to clog anything. It’s not like slathering on coconut oil or something.

**What does the Bourbon Vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
Just a really nice, warm vanilla. Not sweet. Not fake. It’s like the vanilla smell in a bakery but after the cookies are done and everything’s cooled down. It’s subtle but it’s there. Makes my whole nighttime routine feel a bit nicer.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult with the season change, and you’ve tried the usual stuff, this might be worth a shot. It’s just a simple thing in a jar. But it works. I don’t know what else to say. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. That’s all I wanted.
random_tangent: I told my sister about this
